articles.title: Darren England: From Luis Diaz disaster to the Champions League
articles.summary: Referee Darren England shares how he has moved on from the VAR error that stalled his career to the FA Cup final and the Champions League.
articles.body:
If anyone can talk about the highs and lows of being a referee, it is Darren England.

Three years ago, when acting as the video assistant referee (VAR), a blunder in a game between Tottenham and Liverpool stalled his career for months.

Luis Diaz scored for Liverpool , but his goal was flagged as offside. In a lapse of concentration, and despite the VAR image showing Diaz was onside, England said "check complete". The goal remained disallowed.

The South Yorkshire official suddenly found not only himself in the full glare of the media, but his family too.

"Refereeing is about low points and high points," England tells BBC Sport. "It's a rollercoaster of emotions.

"That was a low point. The lowest point, of course."

Today, the 40-year-old's career is revived. He is considered one of the most-trusted referees in the Premier League - both on the field and as a VAR.

Throughout 2026, England has regularly been given some of English football's biggest matches - including Manchester City 's 1-0 win over Chelsea in the FA Cup final.

"So we flip it," England says, moving the conversation along to the game at Wembley. "That was a huge high for me, the pinnacle as a referee."

And on Tuesday, England has been promoted to a VAR in the Champions League for the first time, as Galatasaray take on Stuttgart.

In a 'really difficult place' after Diaz error

The game has changed immeasurably in the 11 years since England swapped his flag for a whistle.

England says referees are now "dressed like RoboCop" as they carry so much additional equipment, such as communication devices.

The biggest change has been the introduction of VAR, which had only been in the Premier League for a few months when England refereed Southampton v Wolves in January 2020.

"It's certainly not changed the way I make decisions," England insists. "If I play on on a penalty decision, some people think the perception is 'oh you're waiting for VAR to get involved'.

"No, I've played on because I don't think it's a penalty.

"But I would rather be driving home from a game now thinking, 'OK, I misread it live, I've had the opportunity to go to the screen and we've corrected it'."

England underlines this, rejecting the notion that referees "don't care about football" when they get a decision wrong.

"It couldn't be further away from the truth," he says. "It's a myth that we go home, we switch off.

"It spoils your weekend if you make a decision that's had a big impact in the game.

"It can spoil it for longer, of course."

From the VAR audio of the Diaz incident, it was clear England and his assistant VAR, Dan Cook were immediately aware they had made a huge mistake.

But the game was only 34 minutes old. They would have to get through the next hour.

"Once I realised I'd made the error, it's a really difficult place to try to forget that and move on," England says.

"I can't just physically stand up and walk out and leave it alone. A lot of resilience was needed - a lot of experience as well."

England described how the VAR hub is a "high pressure" and sanitised environment, with "mental fatigue" taking its toll.

There is no match commentary, just the conversation of the officiating team through their headsets.

"You don't have the atmosphere of the crowd," England says. "You hear some of the crowd sometimes, but it's just a noise.

"When you've had a busy match, you're constantly checking everything. You can come out of the hub sometimes and mentally you're exhausted."

Diaz controversy 'affected my family as well'

What followed was a period of intense media scrutiny which England - and his family - were not prepared for.

The story dominated newspaper headlines, radio phone-ins and social media coverage for days.

Photographers gathered outside his children's school to try to get a picture of him for the newspapers.

One story highlighted the value of his home, while family photographs were taken from his wife's Facebook account.

"The aftermath obviously was really difficult to deal with," England says. "It was challenging because it's the goldfish bowl of the Premier League.

"But when mistakes happen, then you're in the public eye and criticism's inevitably going to come your way.

"That was difficult because it affected my family as well. We had people outside my girls' school, journalists and things like that.

"That then affects you not as a referee, but as a human being."

After the Diaz mistake, England was immediately removed from selection in the Premier League and began a process of rehabilitation.

It would be almost three months before he refereed a top-flight game again, and he did not return to full rotation until February.

It was a longer road back to the VAR room - six-and-a-half months before he was the video official in the Premier League again.

He was eased back in by the Football Association and given a couple of FA Cup ties with Michael Oliver alongside him as the support VAR.

"I did a lot of work with a sports psychologist," England says. "The support, not just from Pro Ref but more importantly family and friends, was really crucial.

"It's about perspective as well. There's a danger that we can think we're saving lives at times, but we also realise how important it is.

"I remained as focused as I could be, working hard, trusting myself, because for all that decision in the Liverpool - Tottenham game, I've made hundreds of other decisions that are correct."

All that focus has paid off, with England the VAR for a decision which was dubbed the 'biggest VAR call ever' as West Ham had a stoppage-time equaliser against Arsenal disallowed on review in May.

England said he "absolutely understood the magnitude" of that decision but "kept calm" under pressure.

Six days later, England took charge of the FA Cup final.

"We're quick to always focus on mistakes and the low points, and how we deal with that," England adds.

"It's one of the targets when you start becoming professional that you want to referee the FA Cup final.

"You only do it once and it's a real honour."

VAR has added a huge amount of additional scrutiny on officials, not just from the press.

England says he will get quizzed by parents on the school run about decisions over the weekend - and not just his own. And then there are the fans online.

"If you want to go searching for good feedback on social media and you're listening to phone-ins, you probably won't find much," England says.

"That can have an impact on how you perform on the field.

"I don't have social media, I made a decision not to. But other people have different preferences and I respect that as well.

"But you have to manage your time accordingly, to be aware that you can never really switch off from football."

To dive or not to dive? Football's big dilemma

Wenger's 'daylight' offside trial unlikely to be extended

Is a double drop from Premier League becoming more common?

England's rise from his "lowest" point has been confirmed by his refereeing appointments.

But it has also been made clear by the respect of his colleagues - which BBC Sport saw first-hand at a referees' training camp at Loughborough University.

Hugh Dallas, the Professional Referee Group director, was at the front of the room, preparing to lead a discussion about decisions from the previous weekend. He paused for a moment, then beckoned forward a referee who, he said, had "become a role model".

That was England, who had recently taken charge of his 100th top-flight game. He was greeted with warm applause as he was handed a Premier League presentation box containing a plaque and a medal.

It is a journey that has taken England from his first match in the village of Royston, five miles outside Barnsley, to the top of the game - twice.

England, who qualified as a referee aged 15, is one of a few to come from inside the game, alongside the likes of Farai Hallam and Sam Allison.

He was working at Barnsley's academy, coaching during training in the week and matches on a Sunday, while refereeing on a Saturday.

Eventually, he had to choose between the two as a professional career - refereeing won.

England first made it to the Premier League as an assistant. Then, in 2015 at the age of 28, he decided to start again in the National League as a referee and work back up.

Within four and a half years, he would take charge of his first Premier League fixture.

"I had the chance of potentially going to tournaments (as an assistant), or do I back myself as a referee?" England says. "Thankfully, it paid off."

England's progress has been closely monitored by Uefa, which has moved him through the levels as a VAR.

After 10 Conference League appointments, and six in the Europa League, this week he is elevated to the Champions League.

"We work extremely hard, and we continue to work extremely hard to stay at that level," England adds.

"Players in the Premier League, they're getting better and better. So we have to keep on improving as well."

After the honour of taking charge of the FA Cup final, does England have any other goals in his career on the field?

"When I don't have targets, that's probably time to come off the field," he says.

"I want to do all the finals that we can do. So obviously, the Carabao Cup, the Championship play-off final.

Three years ago, refereeing an FA Cup final and being a VAR in the Champions League seemed a world away for England.

Now, he's earned the right to have those targets.

articles.title: Aston Villa: Unai Emery aims to prove Villa's worth among the elite against Barcelona in the Champions League
articles.summary: Aston Villa are looking to become the first English team to win at the Nou Camp in almost 20 years.
articles.body:
Unai Emery walked into Villa Park four years ago with two clear aims.

"My dream is to win a trophy with Aston Villa. It's my challenge," he said at his unveiling in November 2022.

"My second dream and my objective could be to play with Aston Villa in Europe. But now, we have to start thinking only the next match because we are not in good position in the table now."

Fast-forward to today and Villa will run out at the Nou Camp to face Barcelona in the Champions League on Tuesday night, having won the Europa League in May and with it ending a 30-year trophy drought.

Emery has already achieved his goals, which has led to natural speculation about the next step - with Villa or elsewhere.

Villa were angered to the point of threatening legal action when Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher said Emery would want to manage an elite club, with Manchester United admirers.

Villa, though, see themselves as a club ready to join the elite - having challenged them in the Premier League and Europe for the past two years - with Emery leading the way.

Emery celebrates his 55th birthday on Tuesday by facing Barca back in his home country.

Carragher's assertion the Spaniard would be open to leaving Villa was naive, given how much Emery controls matters at the club and the success he has had with them, even if it was not the most sensational of opinions.

He signed his most recent contract in May 2024, taking him to 2029, so Villa are protected - but there will ultimately be a new deal following the Europa League triumph.

He has taken Villa up the pecking order, but they are still not at the top of it - though they remain well placed, as the signing of Johan Manzambi from Freiburg showed.

Villa still lost players in the summer to traditionally bigger clubs: Emi Martinez, Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, with Ollie Watkins also leaving for Saudi Arabia . But the changes have given Emery new vigour.

Nights at the Nou Camp give the Spaniard the chance to prove his worth and the progress made at Villa.

"We are constantly seeking new challenges and we want to respond in games against Barcelona to see how far we are from them," he said.

"We won it [the European Cup] in 1982 and right now we are enjoying reminiscing with our fans, playing in this competition again, and trying to repeat that success.

"Barca are favourites because of the present and what they have done over the last 10 years, but they need to confirm their favourite role.

"The way this league stage goes, to end up finishing it in the first eight we need to avoid any kind of surprise.

"There will be times during the season when you walk your own path, but it needs to be clear the second part of the season is when things will be decided.

"Barcelona have six points, we have nine. We need to find out our personality and make the most of our qualities."

Emery was handed carte blanche to change Villa when he was appointed as Steven Gerrard's successor, and he has transformed them from Premier League strugglers to Europa League winners and Champions League challengers.

His methods are intense - players can have several long meetings during the week and can take months to adapt to his demands.

For instance, internally, there is an acceptance it is why Aaron Wan-Bissaka has struggled so far this season, having not had the same level of coaching at West Ham.

The exhaustive nature of his character played a part in former president of football operations Monchi leaving last year , with Emery's close confidante needing a break.

But that meticulousness is also what makes Emery and his teams so effective.

Barcelona sources fear Villa and Emery, citing the struggles of Alejandro Balde and Joao Cancelo's lack of defensive instinct at how Villa can exploit them, given Emery's capacity to plan and pounce on an opponent's weakness.

Emery has earned admirers, including Barcelona boss Hansi Flick, following his achievements at Villa, having already won the Europa League three times with Sevilla and once with Villarreal.

"He is one of the best coaches in Europe and the world. He is very successful," Flick said. "In the way his team plays, you can see a clear structure, and in offence they have different patterns. For me, it is amazing to see his team.

"The start was not easy, but they came back. You can see the confidence they have on the ball, how they play out, and Jackson is at an unbelievable level. For us, it will be a tough game against a good team and, as well, a great coach."

Barca winger Anthony Gordon also called him "one of the best in the world" before the game, even though Emery's record at the Nou Camp is wretched.

He has lost 14 of his 15 games there, having only beaten Barcelona three times in 30 attempts. His last Champions League game at the stadium was Paris St-Germain's collapse as they lost 6-1 in the last 16 , having won the first leg 4-0.

It is a record Emery is eager to change to further cement his status and reputation.

"Everything happened in that match, we know," he said, with no English team winning at the Nou Camp since Liverpool in 2007.

"I started in 2004, playing in Europe 16 years in a row, different competitions, I have learned in all the competitions. In that match I learned so much. The necessity of VAR for football in that moment.

"In my experiences they [his games at the Nou Camp] were giving me a lot of info to learn and get better.

"With the players we are speaking about our experiences together, we have our experience in Europe, in the Champions League two years ago.

"We are facing one of the favourite teams to win the competition, it is a huge challenge. We are confident how we are building the team, how we are facing teams like Barcelona .

"We are here progressing, understanding, setting our demands and competing the level we are, this is the challenge we have."

articles.title: Lisandro Isei, exsecretario técnico del Valencia, habla un año después por primera y última vez... del Valencia: "Orgulloso de mi trabajo"
articles.standfirst: Lo hace a través de su perfil profesional
articles.summary: Lo hace a través de su perfil profesional
articles.body: Prácticamente nadie conoce la voz de Lisandro Isei. Muchos se preguntarán. ¿Quién es? Fue el jefe de scouts del Valencia que contrató hace casi un año Ron Gourlay y durante ese periplo ha ido ejerciendo hasta el punto de convertirse en el responsable de fichajes del Valencia hasta su destitución el 6 de septiembre. Jamás habló en público. Nunca dijo una sola palabra... hasta ayer. Lo ha hecho a través de su cuenta profesional de LinkedIn y en ella se ha expresado en clave de despido del Valencia dos meses después de su fulminante destitución. Tiempo que le ha dado para hacer una reflexión sobre lo vivido y su experiencia en un club como el Valencia. Persona muy recatada y especial, señalan desde la Ciudad deportiva de Paterna, cuya personalidad tenía sus particularidades y que básicamente se centró en la pugna que mantuvo con el exentrenador Carlos Corberán ya que no congeniaron nunca. Uno pedía un perfil y otro, uno muy distinto. Tal fue el devenir de lo que es hoy la plantilla del Valencia. Una nómina de jugadores descompensada y a la que le falta calidad. Pero Isei se ha arrancado a hablar por vez primera en público de la forma que lo ha hecho: "Con siete años el Valencia me tenía pegado a la tele, viviendo todas las emociones que el fútbol puede dar. Acabar trabajando para el club al que apoyé de pequeño ha sido un verdadero privilegio", empieza diciendo. Seguidamente se mete más de lleno en defender su gestión: "Mi tiempo aquí ha llegado a su fin. Estoy orgulloso del trabajo que hicimos y de cómo lo hicimos enfrentando una competencia seria. Incorporamos talento de alto potencial como Ryunosuke Sato y jugadores probados como Dieng y De Haas. Igualmente importante, luchamos para mantener abiertas las vías reales de los jugadores de la Academia y hoy juegan regularmente. Su futuro y el del club se perfilan prometedores", Pero no se quedaba ahí y seguía profundizando en su balance. "Los resultados no eran los que queríamos y en el fútbol los resultados determinan las decisiones. Me consuela saber que mucho del buen trabajo no se refleja a corto plazo. Me voy habiendo aprendido mucho, tanto sobre el juego como sobre mí mismo". Acababa dando las agracias a empleados y jugadores: "Os deseo lo mejor para la temporada y más allá". Frase final es un guiño de acercamiento: "No soc valencianista pel fet d'haver nascut a València, realment va ser el valencianisme el que va nàixer dins de mi. Amunt Valencia" (No soy valencianista por el hecho de haber nacido en Valencia, fue el valencianismo el que nació en mí").

articles.title: Villarreal - PSG: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV y canal del partido de la Champions League
articles.standfirst: La Cerámica recibe al campeón
articles.summary: La Cerámica recibe al campeón
articles.body: El Villarreal y el PSG se enfrentan en un partido correspondiente a la jornada 4 de la fase liga de la Champions League. El encuentro se disputa este martes 3 de noviembre a las 21.00 horas en el Estadio de la Cerámica. El conjunto castellonense afronta una cita de máxima exigencia ante uno de los grandes favoritos al título. Los amarillos suman tres puntos tras las tres primeras jornadas y necesitan reaccionar para acercarse a las posiciones de clasificación, mientras que el equipo parisino comparece en Villarreal con pleno de victorias y situado en primera posición. El equipo dirigido por Íñigo Pérez llega al duelo europeo después de caer en la última jornada liguera frente al Espanyol y con la obligación de hacerse fuerte ante su afición. En la Champions, el Villarreal sumó una victoria ante el Nápoles, por sendas derrotas frente al Borussia Dortmund y el Liverpool, por lo que necesita sumar para no perder terreno en la clasificación. Georges Mikautadze se ha consolidado como una de las principales referencias ofensivas del conjunto groguet, mientras que Gerard Moreno ha llegado entre dudas físicas después de sus problemas musculares recientes. El PSG aterriza en La Cerámica en un gran momento de forma. El vigente campeón de Europa ha ganado sus tres encuentros en la competición continental y presenta una de las mejores cifras goleadoras del torneo. Los de Luis Enrique vienen además de encadenar varios triunfos consecutivos entre todas las competiciones y tratarán de mantener su pleno en la fase liga, a pesar de arrastrar varias bajas confirmadas. El encuentro tendrá además un componente histórico, ya que será el primer enfrentamiento oficial entre Villarreal y PSG en competición europea. Los amarillos buscarán aprovechar el factor campo para sorprender a uno de los equipos más en forma del continente. El partido entre el Villarreal y el PSG se juega el martes 3 de noviembre a las 21.00 horas (horario peninsular español) en el Estadio de la Cerámica. El choque corresponde a la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League 2026-27. El partido entre el Villarreal y el PSG de la jornada 4 de la Champions League se podrá ver por televisión en directo a través de Movistar Liga de Campeones 3. También se podrá seguir el encuentro mediante la plataforma de Movistar Plus+ y a través de la narración de Radio MARCA y los comentarios en directo de MARCA.com. Desde varias horas antes del inicio del encuentro se podrá consultar la última hora de ambos equipos, las alineaciones probables y todas las novedades de una cita clave para las aspiraciones europeas del Villarreal. Tras el partido, estarán disponibles la crónica, las declaraciones de los protagonistas, el análisis y el resumen con las mejores jugadas y los goles del encuentro.

articles.title: Noviembre cura al Madrid más fallón
articles.standfirst: Un mes y medio después de ser el equipo que más ocasiones claras desperdiciaba de Europa, el Madrid ha corregido la puntería, aunque el bajón de Vinicius ensancha la brecha con un Mbappé a pleno rendimiento
articles.summary: Un mes y medio después de ser el equipo que más ocasiones claras desperdiciaba de Europa, el Madrid ha corregido la puntería, aunque el bajón de Vinicius ensancha la brecha con un Mbappé a pleno rendimiento
articles.body: A mediados de septiembre, el Real Madrid cargaba con una gran contradicción en su fútbol: disparaba más que casi nadie, generaba más peligro que el propio Barça y, sin embargo, encabezaba un ranking que ningún equipo quiere liderar, el de las grandes ocasiones falladas en Europa, con 25. El diagnóstico de entonces representaba que el problema de los de Mourinho no estaba en llegar, sino en rematar. Mes y medio después, los números explican la realidad de una mejora palpable por sensaciones y resultados. En aquel primer mes, el equipo blanco malgastó 25 ocasiones manifiestas; en todo el tramo posterior, que supera ya la duración de aquel, apenas ha sumado dos más. La pólvora que se mojaba ha empezado a prender. El Madrid ha pasado de 19 a 28 goles en Liga según datos de Opta, un salto del 47%, y ha elevado su efectividad sobre los disparos entre los tres palos del 32,76% al 36,36%. La clave está en que los goles han crecido a mayor ritmo que los propios disparos: un 47% más de tantos frente a un 33% más de remates a puerta, señal de que el equipo no solo tira más, sino que aprovecha mejor lo que tira. Conviene no confundir la mejora con la coronación a la que aspiran los de Mou. El Madrid dispara mejor que antes, pero sigue a distancia de los más certeros del continente. El Barça convierte uno de cada dos tiros a puerta (51,69%) y la Roma ronda el 44%; el conjunto blanco se queda en ese 36% (uno de cada 2,75) que incluso el Manchester City mejora. La puntería blanca ha dejado de ser una herida a sanar, aunque todavía no sea un arma de precisión. El diagnóstico individual, en cambio, divide a la delantera en dos historias opuestas. Mbappé firma una campaña liguera intachable: 12 goles y un 40% de acierto sobre los disparos a puerta, uno cada dos remates y medio entre palos. Carga, es verdad, con catorce grandes ocasiones falladas, las que más de la plantilla, pero el reproche se desactiva solo cuando se mira el marcador. El que más dispara y más genera es también el que más perdona, y aun así nadie mete tanto. Bellingham lo acompaña con un 40% de acierto y solo dos ocasiones claras desaprovechadas, reconvertido por Mourinho en un futbolista de área que ha recuperado el gol. Y luego está Vinicius, cuyo capítulo discurre a contramano de todo lo demás. Mientras el equipo afinaba la mira, el brasileño la perdía: un gol en siete disparos a puerta, un 14,29% que incluso empeora el 16,67% de septiembre. Dos meses de Liga para sumar un remate entre palos y ningún tanto nuevo. Cinco grandes ocasiones falladas que pesan el triple precisamente porque solo ha celebrado una vez. El Madrid ha curado su puntería colectiva sin que la medicina llegara a su banda izquierda. La reordenación del ataque ha tenido, además, un beneficiario claro en ese mismo sector. En septiembre, Yan Diomande ni siquiera era titular. La posterior sanción de Vinicius —con tres de los cuatro partidos ya cumplidos— le abrió la puerta de la izquierda, y el marfileño la ha cruzado por la puerta grande: tres goles en Liga en cuatro disparos a puerta, un 75% que dibuja a las mil maravillas el estado de gracia del chico. Más allá de la bella factura de los tantos, uno de ellos sirvió para liderar una victoria por la mínima ante el Villarreal. El Madrid de noviembre, en suma, ya no es aquel que generaba para frustrarse. Ha aprendido a transformar, se ha quitado de encima el sambenito del equipo manirroto y afronta el tramo de competición con la sensación de que el esfuerzo, por fin, se traduce en premio.

articles.title: Curvas para Lisandro Martínez en el Manchester United: "En mis tiempos le habrían arrancado la cabeza"
articles.standfirst: Nicky Butt carga contra el rendimiento de Lisandro Martínez y no olvida la bandera de las "Malvinas son argentinas" que lució en el Mundial
articles.summary: Nicky Butt carga contra el rendimiento de Lisandro Martínez y no olvida la bandera de las "Malvinas son argentinas" que lució en el Mundial
articles.body: En Inglaterra no olvidan que Lisandro Martínez, que ha sido muy criticado las últimas semanas por su rendimiento en el Manchester United, exhibiese la bandera "las Malvinas son argentinas" tras ganar 2-1 a Inglaterra durante el Mundial 2026. Nicky Butt, leyenda del Manchester United, ha arremetido duramente contra el central argentino. "Vive en nuestro país y se pone a bailar con una bandera de Argentina durante la Copa del Mundo. ¿Qué estás haciendo?", dijo Butt en el programa 'Piers Morgan Uncensored'. Lisandro Martínez no fue sancionado, pero Argentina recibió una multa de 270.000 euros por su manifestación política. "¿Y luego esperas que la gente te dé palmaditas en la espalda después de haber tenido un mal partido?", apuntó Butt destacando que tras las pobres actuaciones de Lisandro Martínez esta temporada el argentino ya no merece ninguna compasión. Nicky Butt subrayó que "algunas de estas personas tienen que entender algo: ¿y qué importa si ganas 230.000 euros a la semana y conduces tu Rolls-Royce por tu pueblecito creyéndote el rey del mundo? Puedes hacer todo eso cuanto quieras, pero no puedes esperar que te den palmaditas en la espalda cuando juegas tan mal y, encima, te dedicas a criticar a los demás". El exfutbolista recordó las críticas de Lisandro Martínez a los gestores del United, y le acusó que "tiró la toalla". Butt aseguró que si Lisandro Martínez se hubiera comportado así en su época en el United, "en mis tiempos le habrían arrancado la cabeza. Todo el mundo habría dicho: "¿Quién te has creído que eres para hablarme así, viendo el rendimiento que estás ofreciendo? Y, aunque fuera el mejor jugador de Europa, no se puede hablar así de los compañeros de equipo". "No se puede hablar con estos jugadores porque se ofenden enseguida. Luego, tiene la desfachatez de conceder una entrevista y criticar a los responsables del club por el fichaje de jugadores, cuando él mismo ni siquiera está rindiendo bien. Y, si fueran a fichar a alguien, más le valdría tener cuidado, porque él sería uno de los primeros a quienes reemplazarían", declaró. Nicky Butt destacó sobre Lisandro Martínez "ha pasado —no sé por qué— de ser alguien a quien la afición adoraba a ser alguien a quien los seguidores quieren fuera del club; él mismo se ha cavado su propia tumba".

articles.title: Spanish soccer player Jesús de Miguel dies after on-pitch collision
articles.summary: Soccer player Jesús de Miguel has died after an on-field collision during a Spanish second-division match on Monday, his club CD Tenerife has said.
articles.body: Soccer player Jesús de Miguel has died after an on-field collision during a Spanish second-division match on Monday, his club CD Tenerife has said. The Spanish striker sustained injuries after colliding with Andorra’s goalkeeper Jesús Owono in the closing seconds of the Segunda División game. De Miguel had been chasing the ball near the halfway line before Owono – who had come a long way out of his goal – crashed into him at speed while trying to clear it. Owono was instantly shown a red card and sent off for his role in the incident. The Andorra keeper had been walking off the pitch but ran back to his opponent after seeing the severity of the injury. The match was abandoned in the closing minutes as de Miguel received medical support. He initially went down holding his chest following the collision before lying motionless on the pitch. Players from both sides looked devastated. The 30-year-old was then taken straight to hospital and was said to be “stable despite the severity of his condition.” Overnight, though, the club said he had declined “neurologically” and, on Tuesday morning, announced he had died. “Racked with pain, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe that this is true,” the club said in a statement. “There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness. We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones, alongside all of the tinerfeñismo that today weeps for this cruel outcome.” Speaking on Tuesday, CD Tenerife president Felipe Miñambres said: “We are all going through very difficult moments now, of sadness and of not believing what happened. “But we’ll go through the mourning all together, and we’ll be with all the people going through this feeling that should make us be more together.” Andorra also published a statement on Tuesday paying tribute to De Miguel. “Devastated and with broken hearts, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his teammates, friends, and to CD Tenerife,” it said. According to Spanish media, Spain’s National Police have opened an involuntary manslaughter investigation into de Miguel’s death. The High Court of Justice of the Canary Islands told El País that any death that is deemed non-natural requires an investigation. CNN Sports has reached out to the Spanish National Police and the High Court of Justice for comment. Owono deactivated his Instagram account as of Tuesday morning. Tributes De Miguel had signed for Tenerife in the summer of 2025 after spending much of his career in the lower leagues of Spanish soccer. His former teammate at Unionistas de Salamanca CF, Fernando Román, took to X to post a series of photos and a message to his friend: “You were more than a friend… I will never forget you…Rest in Peace” Meanwhile, teams from across the country and the world have also paid tribute to de Miguel. Real Madrid plans to hold a minute of silence ahead of its training session today and said it wanted to “express its condolences and care” to de Miguel’s family and friends, while Barcelona said “we deeply regret the tragic news.” Spain’s soccer federation also announced all Copa del Rey games due to be played on Tuesday had been suspended out of respect. European soccer governing body UEFA also announced that all of its matches this week – including the Champions League where Spanish clubs Atlético Madrid, Barcelona, Villarreal, Real Madrid and Betis are all playing Tuesday and Wednesday – would feature moments of silence in de Miguel’s memory.

articles.summary: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel died after colliding with a goalkeeper during a game; he suffered a cardiac arrest and passed away on Tuesday at the age of 30; Tenerife play in the second tier of Spanish football
articles.body:
"Racked with pain, with ‌a lump in our throats and unable to ​believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic ​passing of Jesus de ⁠Miguel Alameda," the ⁠Spanish second-tier club said.

"There are no words of comfort; there is ‌absolutely nothing that can alleviate this feeling overflowing with sadness."

The match ‌against FC Andorra was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time after De Miguel collapsed following a collision with ⁠away goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who ​had rushed out of ​his area to clear a ​long ball and collided with the striker. Owono was sent off immediately.

Medical staff treated De Miguel on ⁠the pitch for more ​than five minutes before he ​was taken to hospital by ambulance.

Late on Monday night Tenerife issued a statement confirming De Miguel had been admitted to hospital and was initially described as "stable despite the severity of his condition". An update in the early hours of Tuesday morning said his condition had "worsened neurologically".

A club statement concluded: "The family of Jesus de Miguel thanks each and every one of the expressions of support received, and likewise requests, from the heart, the utmost respect for their privacy in these terrible moments."

Opponents Andorra issued a statement on X which read: "With broken hearts and devastated, we want to send our most sincere condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, to all his team-mates, friends, and to CD Tenerife. Rest in peace."

UEFA added that all matches this week will be preceded by a moment of silence in tribute to the player.

On Tuesday, Spanish police said they have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Judicial authorities in the Canary Islands said this was a routine procedure because any death deemed non-natural under Spanish law automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

LaLiga said in a statement: "We wish to express our deep sadness over the tragic passing of Jesús de Miguel Alameda. We share in the grief of his family, his loved ones, and @CDTOficial during these very difficult times. All our affection and support. Rest in peace."

Meanwhile, other Spanish clubs posted messages of condolence to Tenerife and De Miguel's family.

Barcelona said: "From FC Barcelona, we are deeply saddened by the tragic news of the passing of Jesus de Miguel, CD Tenerife player. Our thoughts and support are with his family, friends and loved ones during these difficult times."

Real Madrid said the club "wishes to express its condolences and affection to his family, his team-mates, his club and all his loved ones".

In an interview with Television Canaria , LaLiga president Javier Tebas expressed his profound shock at the news and pledged to make the league's resources available to the club and the family.

Tebas said he would speak with Tenerife to consider postponing their next match, given the circumstances and the immense emotional difficulty of returning to competition this weekend.

He also raised the possibility of organising a joint tribute involving clubs from both divisions of professional football, while emphasising the need for reflection before deciding on specific measures.

Tebas stressed that support for the family and Tenerife must continue not only in these immediate moments, but also throughout the coming weeks.

Aleksander Ceferin, the president of European football's governing body UEFA, said: "We are heartbroken by the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.

"We have searched for words and found only silence. In that silence, our hearts and thoughts are with his family, his team-mates, everyone at Tenerife, and all those who mourn this tragic loss."

Arsenal also held a minute's silence at the start of their training session this morning.

articles.title: Mastantuono explota en Italia: "Es un 10 y medio..."
articles.standfirst: El argentino suma cuatro goles en sus diez primeros partidos con la Fiorentina, iguala un registro de precocidad de Pato y deja atrás los meses complicados que vivió en el Madrid
articles.summary: El argentino suma cuatro goles en sus diez primeros partidos con la Fiorentina, iguala un registro de precocidad de Pato y deja atrás los meses complicados que vivió en el Madrid
articles.body: Franco Mastantuono ha encontrado en Italia el escenario que necesitaba para volver a sonreír. El joven argentino, que llegó a la Fiorentina cedido por el Madrid después de una primera etapa complicada en el Bernabéu, empieza a justificar las expectativas que despertó su fichaje por el conjunto blanco. Franco está encontrando en la Fiorentina los minutos y la confianza que necesitaba para seguir creciendo. El argentino se ha asentado en los planes de Vanoli y cada vez tiene más protagonismo en el equipo italiano. No solo por sus goles, sino también por su participación en el juego y por la responsabilidad que está asumiendo en ataque. Su último tanto llegó ante el Sassuolo. Fue su cuarto gol en los diez partidos que ha disputado en la Serie A... en una victoria que saca al equipo de los puestos de descenso. El argentino se ha convertido en uno de los futbolistas más importantes de la Fiorentina en ataque. Tiene libertad para moverse, busca el uno contra uno y participa cada vez más en las acciones ofensivas. Así las cosas, su arranque en la Serie A le coloca en una estadística histórica junto a Alexandre Pato. Con 19 años y 80 días, es el segundo futbolista más joven en alcanzar cuatro tantos en sus diez primeros encuentros de la competición en la era de los tres puntos por victoria, igualado con Kallon y únicamente por detrás del brasileño, que lo consiguió con 18 años y 154 días. La historia de Mastantuono en Italia, sin embargo, no ha sido una explosión inmediata. El argentino necesitó tiempo para adaptarse a una competición mucho más exigente tácticamente. Después de unos primeros encuentros en los que recibió críticas por su rendimiento y por algunos aspectos de su trabajo defensivo, encontró la manera de quitarse de la presión para empezar a soltarse. Todo arrancó con un hat-trick... aunque después de aquella exhibición llegó un periodo de sequía. Subidas y bajadas, como en el Madrid. Ahora, el tiempo y los minutos parecen estar ayudándole a responder sobre el terreno de juego. Paolo Vanoli ha apostado por él y el futbolista ha ido ganando protagonismo dentro del equipo. "Me gusta mucho jugar metiéndome hacia dentro, sin quedarme siempre pegado a la banda", explicó en Sky. Una pista sobre la libertad que está encontrando en la Fiorentina y que le permite explotar una de sus principales virtudes: su capacidad para conducir, encarar y generar peligro con su zurda. En Florencia, además, ya hay quien se atreve a compararle con algunos de los grandes talentos que han vestido la camiseta viola. Giancarlo Antognoni, una de las mayores leyendas de la entidad, se deshizo en elogios después de su exhibición ante el Venezia. Le definió como un "diez y medio" y encontró similitudes con Roberto Baggio, Rui Costa y Daniel Bertoni. Incluso se atrevió a pronosticar que podía alcanzar los 15 goles en la temporada. "Tiene genio, visión, personalidad y esa despreocupación propia de la juventud", explicó. Son palabras que reflejan el cambio de percepción que empieza a producirse alrededor del argentino. En el Real Madrid no encontró la continuidad necesaria para completar su adaptación al fútbol europeo, mientras que en Florencia está teniendo la oportunidad de equivocarse, aprender y asumir responsabilidades. Todavía queda mucho camino por recorrer, pero sus primeros diez partidos en Italia ya dejan una fotografía significativa.

articles.title: McTominay returns as Penrice earns first Scotland call
articles.summary: Scott McTominay, Kieran Tierney and Che Adams return to the Scotland squad, while there is a first call for James Penrice for the remaining Nations League matches against North Macedonia and Switzerland.
articles.body:
Scott McTominay, Kieran Tierney and Che Adams return to the Scotland squad for the remaining Nations League matches at home to North Macedonia and away to Switzerland.

There is a first call up for James Penrice and uncapped Kristi Montgomery, a late addition last time, retains his place.

Scott McKenna and Kenny McLean miss out through injury, while Lennon Miller, Josh Doig, Colby Donovan and James Wilson drop out.

Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli chose an extended pool of 28 for the first four matches, which included disappointing home defeats to Switzerland and Slovenia.

For these fixtures, the Belgian has gone with 26, sticking with four goalkeepers.

Scotland are third in Group B1 and require a minimum of four points to have any chance of finishing second to feature in the promotion play-offs.

One point would stave off any threat of relegation.

Switzerland lead the way on maximum points, with Slovenia three ahead of Scotland.

Left-back Penrice, 27, has impressed with Rangers since arriving on loan from AEK Athens, while Blackburn Rovers midfielder Montgomery, 22, has started all but one Championship match this season.

Napoli star McTominay has scored four goals in seven outings since recovering from a minor heart procedure.

Adams has doubled his Torino tally for the term with two goals in five Serie A games after a brief lay off with an adductor issue.

Captain Andy Robertson will surpass Sir Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps should the Tottenham full-back feature in both matches on 13 and 16 November.

articles.title: Morata ha vuelto
articles.standfirst: El delantero rompe una sequía de 279 días con un doblete en Valladolid y es la mejor noticia de un Lega
articles.summary: El delantero rompe una sequía de 279 días con un doblete en Valladolid y es la mejor noticia de un Lega
articles.body: Dentro de la dolorosa derrota del Leganés en Valladolid (4-3), los pepineros encontraron una noticia para la esperanza: Álvaro Morata ha vuelto. El delantero madrileño necesitó poco más de media hora sobre el césped para marcar dos goles, recuperar la sonrisa y demostrar que todavía tiene mucho que aportar al conjunto de Luis Carrión. Morata puso fin a una sequía de 279 días sin marcar. Su último tanto había llegado el 27 de enero, cuando todavía defendía la camiseta del Como italiano, ante la Fiorentina en la Copa de Italia. Más de nueve meses después, el delantero volvió a encontrarse con el gol y lo hizo por partida doble, estrenándose además como goleador del Leganés. Saltó al terreno de juego en el minuto 55, con el marcador prácticamente sentenciado (4-1), y cambió la cara ofensiva de su equipo. Marcó el primero en el 68’, con un disparo de zurda, y completó su doblete en el tiempo añadido. Se mostró participativo, con confianza y con esa ambición que tanto necesitaba recuperar. Fue, sin duda, lo mejor de una tarde complicada para los pepineros. El problema es que los goles de Morata no fueron suficientes. El Leganés volvió a mostrar una preocupante fragilidad defensiva, encajando cuatro tantos y concediendo demasiadas facilidades a su rival. El equipo genera ocasiones y empieza a encontrar soluciones en ataque, pero necesita mejorar mucho atrás si quiere cambiar su dinámica. Luis Carrión tiene ahora una buena noticia sobre la que construir. Recuperar la mejor versión de Morata puede resultar fundamental para el futuro del Leganés. El delantero ya ha respondido con goles. Ahora necesita que el resto del equipo, especialmente en defensa, le acompañe.

articles.body:
Over 26,000 professional footballers have chosen their best men's and women's teams, with 26 finalists for both selections now revealed.

The 11 players who received the most votes in their position will make the final team.

Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice are the English representatives on the men's shortlist.

The women's shortlist features seven English players: Hannah Hampton, Lucy Bronze, Alex Greenwood, Ella Toone, Aggie Beever-Jones, Chloe Kelly and Alessia Russo .

Unsurprisingly, Lionel Messi (18) and Cristiano Ronaldo (16) lead the way with most appearances for the men's XI.

England Lioness Bronze, meanwhile, has been voted into the women's team eight times - a remarkable achievement given the women's award was only launched in 2016.

articles.title: Las consecuencias que puede tener la entrada de Owono a Jesús de Miguel: qué dice la vía deportiva y la penal
articles.standfirst: Dos abogadas penalistas explican a MARCA qué recorrido puede tener el caso y por qué piden prudencia hasta que haya una investigación
articles.summary: Dos abogadas penalistas explican a MARCA qué recorrido puede tener el caso y por qué piden prudencia hasta que haya una investigación
articles.body: El fútbol español amaneció este martes con una noticia triste. Jesús de Miguel Alameda, delantero del CD Tenerife, falleció en el Hospital Universitario Nuestra Señora de Candelaria, según comunicó el club. El jugador había sido ingresado el lunes tras una acción en el tiempo añadido del partido ante el Andorra. La jugada, en la que coincidieron el delantero blanquiazul y el guardameta del Andorra, Jesús Owono, terminó con la expulsión del portero. De Miguel recibió asistencia médica en el césped y fue trasladado al hospital. Han surgido muchas preguntas sobre lo que puede pasar a partir de ahora, tanto en los comités deportivos como, llegado el caso, en los juzgados. Para resolverlas, MARCA ha hablado con Blanca Alguacil, abogada especialista en Derecho Penal del Ilustre Colegio de Abogados de Madrid (Alguacil Rojo Abogados) y María Barbancho, CEO de Barbancho Legal y experta en derecho penal. María Barbancho pone el foco en una cuestión de fondo: hasta dónde llega el riesgo que se asume al practicar un deporte de contacto. "El fútbol es un deporte de contacto, y quien lo practica sabe que en un campo se reciben golpes que fuera de él serían impensables", explica. Según detalla, el Derecho Penal parte de esa misma idea y no interviene en las lesiones que forman parte del juego, aunque sean graves, porque entiende que ese riesgo lo asumen todos los que salen a jugar. La dificultad, añade, está en saber dónde está ese límite. Y advierte contra las conclusiones precipitadas: "Eso no quiere decir que detrás de cada entrada que termina en tragedia haya un delito, y menos aún que pueda afirmarse a partir de unas imágenes". A juicio de Alguacil, "hay que separar la opinión que cada uno pueda tener de una jugada de lo que tiene, o no, relevancia penal". Y esa valoración, insiste, no corresponde ni a los periodistas ni a los abogados, sino a un juez. Se trata, resume, de un suceso extraordinario y muy trágico, sobre el que hay que hablar con mucha prudencia. Alguacil recuerda que "en Derecho penal no podemos partir de la gravedad del resultado para deducir automáticamente la existencia de un delito". Y, en caso de que se incoen diligencias de investigación, "será el juez instructor quien, a la vista de las pruebas y de las circunstancias del caso, deba valorar si existen indicios suficientes de responsabilidad penal". Hasta entonces, cualquier calificación jurídica sería precipitada. La penalista distingue con claridad los dos ámbitos. Por un lado está la infracción deportiva, que ya figura en el acta arbitral y que juzgarán los comités. Por otro, es una cuestión diferente que esto vaya a trasladarse a una acción penal y que tenga relevancia en la misma. En ese equilibrio caben dos derechos a la vez: el del portero a defenderse y el de la familia, o incluso el club, a acudir a los tribunales si lo consideran oportuno. Por eso, señala, nadie debería dar por cerrada ninguna conclusión antes de tiempo. Preguntada por el encaje legal, Alguacil explica que el Código Penal recoge en su artículo 142 el homicidio por imprudencia, en dos modalidades: grave (castigada con prisión de uno a cuatro años) y menos grave (con multa de tres a dieciocho meses). Pero subraya que la existencia de ese artículo "no significa que esta acción vaya a considerarse penalmente reprochable" Lo primero, explica, "sería una investigación judicial que determine exactamente qué pasó, empezando por la autopsia que establezca la causa del fallecimiento", y si este guarda relación con la acción del partido. Después habría que valorar "si existió una negligencia grave, es decir, si se omitieron las normas más básicas del deber de cuidado". Para explicarlo, la abogada recurre a un ejemplo habitual en su trabajo, el de las negligencias médicas: un error profesional no implica intención de causar daño, pero puede tener consecuencias legales según su gravedad. Su opinión, que ella misma presenta como tal y con la cautela de que todavía falta toda la investigación, es que "sería difícil acreditar esa imprudencia grave en una acción de juego". En paralelo, el caso tiene su propio cauce deportivo. El Reglamento General de LaLiga regula la competición (calendario, clubes y derechos), pero la disciplina de los jugadores corresponde al Comité de Competición de la RFEF, que aplica su Código Disciplinario. Su resolución se puede recurrir ante el Comité de Apelación y, después, ante el Tribunal Administrativo del Deporte (TAD). El punto de partida será el acta arbitral. A partir de ella, el Comité tendrá que decidir cómo califica la acción. Estas son las horquillas que se contemplan: La sanción deportiva se impone por la conducta y no por el resultado, aunque el Comité tendrá en cuenta todas las circunstancias al valorar los hechos. Las respuestas llegarán con los plazos de cada vía: primero los comités deportivos y, si alguien decide acudir a ellos, los tribunales. Hasta entonces, el fútbol español se queda con lo único que no admite discusión: la despedida de Jesús de Miguel, un futbolista de 30 años al que hoy lloran su familia, su club y todo el deporte. Las respuestas llegarán con los plazos de cada vía. Hasta entonces, como resume María Barbancho, la muerte de Jesús de Miguel "nos obliga a pensar con calma qué grado de riesgo estamos dispuestos a seguir considerando parte del fútbol". Y el fútbol español se queda con lo único que no admite discusión: la despedida de un futbolista de 30 años al que hoy lloran su familia, su club y todo el deporte.

articles.summary: Ninguno de los dos viaja a Atenas para medirse al AEK
articles.body: Arda Güler y Aurelien Tchoauméni no viajan a Atenas para medirse al AEK. En el Real Madrid están extremando las precauciones para evitar las lesiones musculares, algo que están consiguiendo este curso tras unas temporadas en las que el club blanco lo ha pasado realmente mal en este sentido. Además, Mou quiere ganar a más jugadores para la causa, de ahí que estas rotaciones le sirvan para intentar enganchar a más futbolistas y que todos se sientan importantes. articles.title: Khadija Shaw among big names to miss out on FifPro World XI
articles.summary: Eyebrows are raised at the announcement of the FifPro Women's World XI shortlist with several big names missing.
articles.body:
Eyebrows were raised on Monday when the FifPro Women's World XI shortlist was unveiled and several big names were missing.

The 26-player shortlist was voted for by players from around the world and is the only award decided solely by fellow footballers.

It is considered prestigious as a result but when the list dropped and five of the top 10 Ballon d'Or finishers were not included, it understandably caused a stir.

Among the notable absentees was Manchester City's top scorer Khadija Shaw, who finished third in the Ballon d'Or.

Malawi star Temwa Chawinga and Haiti's Melchie Dumornay were also shock omissions, along with Barcelona's Caroline Graham Hansen and Denmark captain Pernille Harder.

However, England trio Ella Toone, Chloe Kelly and Aggie Beever-Jones are surprise inclusions.

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

The world XI shortlist was voted for by 6,511 women's footballers from 64 countries via an online system with FifPro.

The finalists are the players who received the most votes judged on their period between 4 August 2025 and 16 August 2026.

All players had to feature at least 20 times during that period to be eligible for nomination and the winners will be unveiled on Monday, 9 November (13:00 GMT).

The world XI will consist of one goalkeeper, three defenders, three midfielders and three forwards who all received the most votes in their positions.

The remaining spot will be taken by the outfield player, from any position, with the next highest number of votes.

Votes for a player in more than one position (for example, if they are named as a midfielder or a forward), are combined.

It is not the first time the shortlists have been controversial.

Last year, Arsenal and Spain midfielder Mariona Caldentey was not included in the FifPro World XI despite coming runner-up in the Ballon d'Or.

In 2024, when 7,000 women's footballers voted, four of the top five in the Ballon d'Or were not shortlisted, including the often overlooked Graham Hansen.

Instead, five Lionesses made the cut despite not winning a major trophy that year or having any finalists in the Ballon d'Or top 10.

This time around the WSL's Player of the Year Shaw missed out. She helped Manchester City win a league and FA Cup double as their top scorer with 21 goals in 22 games.

Meanwhile, the inclusions of England trio Toone, Kelly and Beever-Jones were controversial with all three initially failing to make the most recent Lionesses squad.

Chelsea's Beever-Jones scored just seven goals in all competitions for club and country during the period of voting, while Toone and Kelly both struggled for form and fitness in that time.

In contrast, England team-mates Lauren Hemp of Manchester City and Chelsea's Lauren James were in good form and impressed for their clubs but missed out.

However, Lyon striker Ada Hegerberg is in. The 2018 Ballon d'Or winner did not score in the knockout stages of the Women's Champions League and was not a guaranteed starter for Lyon in the first period of voting in what was a below-par season for her standards.

articles.title: Felipe Miñambres, roto por la muerte de Jesús de Miguel: "Vamos a necesitar ayuda profesional"
articles.standfirst: El presidente del CD Tenerife, completamente abatido tras la muerte de Jesús de Miguel, admite que el club, la plantilla y las familias de los jugadores necesitarán apoyo psicológico para afrontar una tragedia que ha conmocionado al fútbol español
articles.summary: El presidente del CD Tenerife, completamente abatido tras la muerte de Jesús de Miguel, admite que el club, la plantilla y las familias de los jugadores necesitarán apoyo psicológico para afrontar una tragedia que ha conmocionado al fútbol español
articles.body: El CD Tenerife sigue intentando asimilar el golpe más duro de su historia reciente. Horas después del trágico fallecimiento de Jesús de Miguel, el máximo accionista del club, Rayco García, y el presidente, Felipe Miñambres, comparecieron visiblemente afectados desde el Hospital Nuestra Señora de La Candelaria para transmitir el duelo que atraviesa toda la entidad blanquiazul. Con semblantes devastados y entre lágrimas, ambos dirigentes trasladaron el dolor de una familia que todavía no logra comprender lo ocurrido. Rayco García confirmó que el cuerpo del futbolista será trasladado en los próximos días a Navahermosa (Toledo), cumpliendo así el deseo expreso de sus familiares, y anunció un acto de despedida para este sábado en el Heliodoro Rodríguez López. "Nos enfrentamos a una situación sin precedentes. Estamos muy dolidos, el tinerfeñismo está de luto. Es muy difícil de aceptar", confesó el dirigente, antes de hacer un llamamiento a la afición para arropar a la familia y al equipo en uno de los momentos más dramáticos que recuerda el club. "La vida nos ha golpeado a todos, pero somos una gran familia y vamos a salir adelante", añadió. Sin embargo, fue Felipe Miñambres quien puso voz a la enorme dimensión emocional de la tragedia. El presidente del Consejo de Administración reconoció que la muerte de Jesús de Miguel ha dejado al vestuario, a los dirigentes y a todo el entorno blanquiazul en una situación límite. "Es un día muy triste para todo el sentimiento blanquiazul y para el fútbol mundial. Es una situación no vivida, que un jugador muera así en un terreno de juego", señaló con la voz quebrada. Miñambres admitió que el impacto psicológico será profundo y que el club necesitará apoyo especializado para afrontar las próximas semanas. "Estamos en momentos de debilidad, de tristeza, de no creer lo que ha pasado. Pasaremos el luto y esto nos hará estar más unidos. Tenemos que pasar una semana de luto, vamos a necesitar ayuda profesional, nosotros, los jugadores y sus familias", aseguró. El máximo mandatario tinerfeñista también quiso extender ese mensaje a los aficionados, igualmente golpeados por una pérdida que ha sacudido al fútbol español. "Tenemos que hacer el homenaje que 'Demi' se merece. Lo llevaremos siempre en el corazón. Es una desgracia grandísima la que hemos sufrido", concluyó. Mientras el Tenerife trata de encontrar fuerzas para afrontar el dolor, la isla se prepara para despedir a uno de los suyos en un homenaje que promete convertirse en una de las imágenes más emotivas y sobrecogedoras de la historia del club. Jesús de Miguel ya forma parte para siempre de la memoria del tinerfeñismo.

articles.title: Middle East conflict hits Saudi football: Pro League postpones matches after Asian Cup delay; Ronaldo also affected
articles.summary: The impact of the escalating conflict in the Middle East on Saudi football has widened, with the Saudi Pro League (SPL) postponing Matchweek 13 after the
articles.body: The impact of the escalating conflict in the Middle East on Saudi football has widened, with the Saudi Pro League (SPL) postponing Matchweek 13 after the 2027 AFC Asian Cup was pushed back by almost a year amid security concerns and logistical challenges in the region.The SPL announced the decision on Tuesday, just two days before the scheduled start of the gameweek, saying it would review the domestic fixture calendar following the change in dates of the continental tournament. The new dates for the postponed league matches will be announced once the review is complete."The decision comes as part of a wider review of the 2026-27 RSL (Roshn Saudi League) fixture schedule, with the revised Asian Cup dates creating additional flexibility in the domestic football calendar," the league said in a statement.The postponement follows the AFC's decision to move the Asian Cup from its original January 7-February 5, 2027 window to December 23, 2027-January 21, 2028. The tournament, which will feature 24 teams across eight venues in Riyadh, Jeddah and Khobar, has been affected by developments in the region, including security concerns, travel disruptions and logistical complications.The decision came after months of uncertainty over whether Saudi Arabia could host the competition as planned. The situation has been particularly tense following deadly attacks on the kingdom, including a strike on Riyadh's international airport last month that killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement claimed responsibility for the attack.Ronaldo's Al-Nassr among clubs affected by continental disruptionsThe uncertainty has also affected Saudi clubs competing in the AFC Champions League Elite, with Cristiano Ronaldo's Al-Nassr among those experiencing interruptions to their continental campaign.Al-Nassr's home fixture against UAE side Al-Wasl was postponed after the visitors did not travel to Riyadh. The club's previous home match in the competition, against Uzbekistan's Neftchi Fergana, had also been delayed by an hour after a security alert was issued amid reports of missile attacks.Ronaldo was subsequently left out of Al-Nassr's squad for the away match against Uzbekistan's Pakhtakor. However, head coach Ange Postecoglou described the decision as a rest, citing the demands of the schedule and travel rather than directly linking it to the security situation."We've rested Cristiano, Kingsley Coman and Mohamed Simakan given the pressure of matches and the amount of travel involved," Postecoglou said.Ronaldo had scored a hat-trick in a Saudi Pro League match the previous week, taking his career tally to 985 goals. Al-Nassr are also chasing their first Asian continental title, although they have made a difficult start to the Champions League campaign.Wider sporting calendar hit by regional uncertaintyThe Asian Cup postponement is the latest major sporting disruption linked to the conflict. The Saudi Arabian Formula One Grand Prix was cancelled this season, while the Bahrain race was relocated to Malaysia. The WTA Finals, meanwhile, were moved from Saudi Arabia to Indian Wells in the United States.For the SPL, the immediate priority is to accommodate the revised Asian Cup calendar while managing an already disrupted domestic season. The league has rescheduled several fixtures for logistical reasons, and the latest decision adds another adjustment to its 2026-27 schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Spanish Police Investigating After Soccer Player Dies Following On-Field Collision
articles.summary: BARCELONA, Spain (AP) — Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter after a soccer player died following an on-field collision with the opposing team's goalkeeper in a second-division match.
articles.body:
BARCELONA, Spain (AP) — Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter after a soccer player died following an on-field collision with the opposing team's goalkeeper in a second-division match.

Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel died after he suffered cardiac arrest following the on-field collision, his club said Tuesday. He was 30.

De Miguel was challenging for the ball near midfield on Monday when he was struck in the chest by Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, who came running from the opposite direction in an apparent attempt to make a clearance. Owono was shown a straight red card for the incident, which happened in added time.

The country's National Police said Tuesday that an investigation was opened. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation.

De Miguel was taken to a hospital and the match, tied 2-2, was abandoned after the incident.

The club located on Spain's Canary Islands said it was "heartbroken."

The heavy collision happened when Owono rushed out of his area all the way to midfield to challenge for a long ball that De Miguel was trying to reach.

De Miguel initially curled on his knees, clutching his torso for a few seconds, before he fell over onto his back, with his arms falling to his sides.

Owono was walking off the field after being shown the red card but turned around and joined the other players rushing to check on De Miguel.

The goalkeeper's Instagram account, which had nearly 30,000 followers, had been deactivated on Tuesday.

De Miguel, a Madrid native, began his senior career with Leganés B in 2015 and subsequently played for a number of lower-division clubs in Spain. He joined Tenerife last year.

Spanish media said De Miguel is survived by his wife and their daughter.

"There are no words of comfort," the club statement read. "There is absolutely nothing that can alleviate this profound sense of sorrow. We stand with his devastated family, his loved ones, and the entire Tenerife community."

Andorra, which is owned by former Barcelona star Gerard Piqué, also offered its condolences, along with other clubs, the Spanish soccer federation and La Liga.

"We wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesús de Miguel, to all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife. May he rest in peace," Andorra said in a statement.

Piqué said on X: "I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesús."

The players of Real Madrid held a minute of silence for De Miguel during training, while fellow topflight club Espanyol postponed the presentation of its new coach.

Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé said on social media: "So much sadness. There are no words."

Argentina great Lionel Messi said on Instagram: "There are no words. My condolences and lots of strength to all his family and friends."

English clubs Manchester United and Liverpool joined in offering their condolences on social media.

The Spanish soccer federation postponed two Copa del Rey matches and one Copa de la Reina matches scheduled for later on Tuesday.

Life-threatening injuries from collisions in soccer are extremely rare.

Last year in Spain, a 19-year-old goalkeeper died from head injuries suffered during a collision in a fifth-division match. Colindres goalkeeper Raúl Ramírez had two cardiorespiratory arrests, one on the field and then in the ambulance while being transported to a hospital. He was declared brain dead two days later.

In 2001, Ukrainian goalkeeper Serhiy Perkhun died from head injuries sustained in a collision during a match while playing for CSKA Moscow.

Malaga goalkeeper José Antonio Gallardo died in January 1987, more than three weeks after a collision with Celta Vigo forward Baltazar in a second-division game.
authors: Joseph Wilson and Tales Azzoni, Associated Press

articles.title: Do sports stars have the right to free speech?
articles.summary: The Mbappe controversy demonstrates how market power in sport is being used to enforce conformity.
articles.body:
French football superstar Kylian Mbappe recently landed in trouble over a meme. Discussing an image that apparently superimposed his face on Mao Zedong’s, he referred to the late Chinese leader as someone he thought was a dictator, without naming Mao.

The offhand remark became an international controversy. Chinese sponsors withdrew their support. State television suspended La Liga broadcasts. Apologies followed from Mbappe and his club, Real Madrid, while the league expressed regret over the offence caused.

Mbappe was riffing on one of the running jokes about his outsized influence over his clubs and teammates. He was not delivering a considered assessment of Chinese history. Yet the response turned a passing remark into a test of respect for an entire nation.

Mbappe is not the first athlete to discover how quickly political sensitivities become instruments of discipline. A decade ago, American football star Colin Kaepernick knelt during the United States national anthem to protest systemic racism and police killings of Black people, and was effectively frozen out of the National Football League.

In May, after Spanish footballer Lamine Yamal waved a Palestinian flag during Barcelona’s title celebrations, Israel’s defence minister, Israel Katz, accused him of inciting hatred and demanded that the club distance itself from the gesture.

Kaepernick and Yamal made deliberate statements. Mbappe made a joke. Yet the distinction offered the latter little protection. An athlete need not deliberately enter politics to discover how tightly his speech is policed.

Mbappe’s extraordinary visibility gives him influence and makes him commercially valuable. But the commercial relationships that make him valuable also hand others the means to discipline him.

The logic is an old one. In ancient Greece, victorious athletes could receive substantial rewards from their cities, including money, meals at public expense and civic honours. Sporting success could open a path to political influence, and their achievements brought prestige to the communities that claimed them.

But the claim could become possessive. According to the ancient Greek geographer and writer Pausanias, the runner Astylus, originally associated with Croton, later proclaimed himself a Syracusan when competing at the Olympic Games. His former compatriots responded by pulling down his statue and converting his house into a prison.

Today, sporting institutions make similar claims on the people whose achievements they celebrate. The athlete represents the nation, embodies the club, carries the sponsor’s values. Each relationship becomes a reason to keep an inconvenient thought to oneself. As Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho put it, “Often the best thing you can do is keep your mouth shut, because there’s danger in so many things you say or comment on.”

When a single remark threatens access to a market, the club and the league acquire a financial interest in treating it as misconduct, and the pressure to recant can be extreme. When a state broadcaster suspends an entire league, it punishes thousands of players, staff and viewers who had nothing to do with the remark, effectively holding them hostage to one man’s apology. That is market power being used to enforce conformity.

This is where the contradictions of celebrity become especially apparent. Sporting businesses sell courage, authenticity and individual character. They encourage audiences to identify with the person behind the performance. But the expression of that character becomes a problem when it threatens another part of the business.

The athlete is invited to be themselves, subject to approval.

Further, audiences add their own pressure. We increasingly expect sports stars to address moral and political questions, and we judge their silence as well as their speech. Fame does carry obligations. But athletic excellence does not confer political wisdom, and prominence is not a qualification. If we want courage from athletes, we must also confront the institutions that make courage professionally dangerous.

Mbappe’s case is revealing precisely because he was not taking a heroic stand. The freedom to speak cannot depend on an athlete being historically knowledgeable, perfectly articulate or deliberately brave. It must leave room for an uncertain remark and a foolish joke, as well as a carefully planned protest.

However, it is clear that freedom does not confer immunity from critique. Fans can disagree loudly, and athletes should answer for objectionable speech. But the test should be whether a remark harms people, not whether it embarrasses a state or threatens a balance sheet.

The supposed neutrality of sport helps to hide these demands for conformity. Flags, anthems and governments’ pursuit of prestige already fill sporting spectacles with political meaning. Athletes’ independent expression, on the other hand, attracts demands for silence when it disrupts those authorised messages.

Yet though bringing honour to a community, a champion’s achievement does not give that community ownership over them. Clubs can purchase sporting services. Sponsors can purchase advertising. Neither transaction entitles anyone to dictate an athlete’s convictions.

If sporting institutions insist on selling us the person behind the performance, they must accept that the person has a voice of their own.
